methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 8 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+. The valuation universe consists of 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers in robotics and manufacturing, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity.

The Stage-Progression method is the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $575M as a baseline value proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $690M. The Peer-Median method cannot be reliably applied due to insufficient narrow peer data; while 8 same-sector comparables exist, filtering by stage, adjacency, or valuation tier produced fewer than the minimum 3 datapoints needed for statistical validity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $586M to $793M, with a median estimate of $690M. This range reflects the upper and lower bounds of the stage-progression methodology but carries meaningful uncertainty. The primary constraint is reliance on a single method; a more robust triangulation would require either expanded peer comparability data or additional valuation anchors such as revenue multiples or DCF outputs. Given the data available, the $690M median represents the most defensible point estimate, though investors should recognize this reflects capital-raise progression rather than market-based peer validation.
